one_liner: Rust/Wasm fine-grained-reactive web UI framework; about 1.46x faster than React 19.2 hooks in js-framework-benchmark, slower than vanilla JS.
what_it_does: Full-stack Rust web framework: components written with a JSX-like view! macro (or a builder API) compile to WebAssembly for client-side rendering, or render HTML on the server with hydration, streaming Suspense and isomorphic server functions. It is not a drop-in for React; you rewrite the UI in Rust and use signals (signal, Memo, Effect, Resource) instead of hooks.
how_it_is_fast: Fine-grained reactivity in the SolidJS style: each component runs once, creates real DOM nodes and wires signals to the exact text node, class or attribute that depends on them, so there is no virtual-DOM re-render or diff (reactive_graph plus the tachys renderer). Keyed lists use the <For> component's keyed diff, Selector gives O(1) selection changes, the template! macro renders static HTML into a <template> at compile time and clones it, and the optional delegation feature installs one event listener per event type instead of one per element. Release builds use LTO, codegen-units=1, panic=abort and wasm-opt -O4.
when_to_use: You want to write a browser UI in Rust (shared types with an Axum or Actix backend, server functions) and need DOM update speed at least as good as React's.

Large keyed tables or lists with reorder, partial-update and select patterns: in the suite Leptos takes 0.136x React hooks' time on swap rows, 0.574x on select row, 0.776x on partial update and 0.666x on create 10,000 rows.
SSR plus hydration or streaming HTML apps where the same Rust components render on server and client.

Teams already on Rust that are choosing between Rust UI frameworks: Leptos is within a few percent of Sycamore, Dioxus and rust-dominator on suite speed and has the largest ecosystem of the Rust options.
when_not_to_use: If raw DOM speed is the goal and JavaScript is acceptable: on the same suite Leptos takes 1.246x vanillajs-keyed's time, 1.128x Solid 1.9.3, 1.135x Inferno and 1.052x Svelte 5.42.1 (derived from page data).

Startup- or memory-sensitive pages: first paint 239.6 ms vs React's 226.6 ms, ready memory 1.77 vs 1.19 MB, run memory 5.45 vs 4.37 MB, and about 190 kB uncompressed / 48.8 kB compressed bundle vs Solid's 11.5 / 4.5 kB.
Workloads dominated by creating or clearing rows: create 1,000 rows is 1.06x React's time, append is a tie, clear rows is 15.6 ms vs 8.7 ms for vanilla JS.

Projects that need long-term active development: the May 2026 status update (issue #4707) calls Leptos feature-complete and 'lightly maintained going forward', with 0.9 a semver-breaking cleanup release.
Sites that require a strict Content-Security-Policy: the suite tags the Leptos entry with note #1139 (does not pass strict CSP).

integration.dependencies: wasm-bindgen, web-sys and js-sys for the browser; reactive_graph, tachys, leptos_macro, server_fn and related workspace crates; getrandom with its JS backend if the app uses rand on wasm; build with cargo-leptos, Trunk or wasm-pack
integration.min_toolchain: Rust 1.88 (workspace rust-version, edition 2024 on main); the measured build used the 'nightly' feature, which needs a nightly toolchain
integration.platforms: Browsers with WebAssembly (wasm32-unknown-unknown) for client rendering; any Rust server target for SSR
integration.thread_safety: Signals are Copy + 'static handles owned by a reactive owner; Arc* variants (ArcRwSignal) are Send + Sync for server use; browser rendering is single-threaded

gotchas: The measured build is not the default configuration: the suite builds Leptos 0.7 with the 'nightly' and 'delegation' features (main's own examples/js-framework-benchmark says 'for actual benchmarking, add nightly and delegation features') and uses the template! macro; a stock csr build attaches one listener per element.

The 1.46x geometric-mean win over React is mostly one row: React hooks takes 89.7 ms on swap rows against 11-14.6 ms for Leptos, Solid, Inferno, Svelte and vanilla JS. Without swap rows the geometric mean is 0.837x React's time, about 1.19x faster (derived from page data).

The suite measures Leptos 0.7 from a prebuilt bundle checked into the benchmark repo (no Cargo.lock, 'build-prod is a no-op'), while crates.io's latest stable is 0.8.22 and main moved to 0.9.0-beta2 on 2026-10-10; current versions are unmeasured.
COMMON_BUGS.md warns that writing to a signal from an Effect creates update chains and can loop forever, and that value=... on <input> only sets the default value (use prop:value).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick Leptos over Yew when speed matters (Yew 0.23 takes about 1.20x Leptos's time, Yew hooks about 1.51x) and over Sycamore, Dioxus or rust-dominator (all within 4% of Leptos) when you want SSR, streaming and server functions in one framework; pick hand-written wasm-bindgen code (Leptos takes 1.171x its time) or Silkenweb (1.099x) when only the last bit of DOM speed and lower memory matter (derived from page data).
verified_claims_summary: In krausest/js-framework-benchmark (Chrome 154 snapshot, CPU model not stated), leptos-v0.7.0-keyed needs 0.684x the time of react-hooks-v19.2.0-keyed as an unweighted geometric mean of the medians of nine table benchmarks, with swap rows (12.2 vs 89.7 ms) driving most of the gap; create 1,000 rows is slower (25.1 vs 23.6 ms) and it is 1.246x slower than vanilla JS. The README's only performance claim is qualitative ('much faster ... than Yew'), and the suite shows Leptos about 1.20x faster than Yew 0.23.
status_note: Active and widely used (21.4k stars, 5.2M crates.io downloads, last commit 2026-10-10 merging the 0.9 branch) but declared feature-complete and lightly maintained by its author in May 2026; MIT-licensed and usable as a crate.
